title: The Cisco Kid
paragraphs: Cisco and Pancho ride the Southwest confronting outlaws and helping people in trouble, represented here mainly by the Jack Mather and Harry Lang syndicated run plus a rare earlier network broadcast.

Western adventure series derived from O. Henry’s Cisco Kid property. Production history is separated from later syndicated air dates. Frozen GRH has 186 playable objects, including three undated items and 24 dated after the researched 1956 original-production endpoint.

GRH documents the program through Mutual network era (October 2, 1942 to February 14, 1945) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Regional Mutual-Don Lee revival (January 1, 1946 to December 31, 1946) on [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]], Ziv prerecorded syndication production (January 1, 1947 to December 31, 1956) on [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]], and Post-production syndicated airings (January 1, 1957 to June 24, 1958).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Harry Lang (performer on 149 recordings), Jack Mather (performer on 149 recordings), Herb Butterfield (performer on 4 recordings), Lou Krugman (performer on 4 recordings), Barton Yarborough (performer on 3 recordings), Herb Vigran (performer on 3 recordings), and Bill Bouchey (performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]] (originated at station), [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.070a5b7dde24b155|Ziv]] (syndicated by), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include sheriffs, law and frontier justice, guns, shootings and armed violence, robbery and theft, gold, mining and prospecting, ranching and cattle, and outlaws and banditry.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including O. Henry outlaw transformed into heroic Cisco Kid franchise, Postwar prerecorded transcription syndication, and Mexican/Latino Western hero in mid-century popular radio.
